seo.title: Cropstar — software that explains instead of prescribes
seo.description: Open-source farm software for regenerative agriculture. Every number carries its uncertainty, its source and its drivers. Scenarios, never recommendations.
seo.ogTitle: Cropstar — understand your field, decide for yourself
seo.ogDescription: Open-source farm software for regenerative agriculture. Learning by doing, with the consequences made visible.

hero.lead: Cropstar will not tell you which variety to sow, when to fertilise or what to spray. It lays bare what is happening in your field, so you can interpret your own ecosystem. For anyone tired of blindly following decisions others made for them.

facts.numbersValue: a band, a source and a reason
facts.decisionValue: with the person in the field

independence.title: Independence begins with understanding
independence.p1: Almost every decision in the field comes with a recommendation – often from someone with something to sell. That is convenient while the season follows the plan. When it does not, the question of why remains.
independence.p2: A resilient farm is built not on ready-made answers, but on understanding how water, nutrients, plants and soil interact.
independence.p3: No software can replace that understanding, and Cropstar does not try. It wants to get the ball rolling: make relationships visible, play consequences through, keep a record of what you observed. The decision stays where it belongs.

principles.title: What Cropstar deliberately does differently
principles.lead: Open in its development, transparent in its results and free from ready-made judgements.

openness.title: Developed openly, shaped together
openness.body: Open source and independent. Developed by and for people in agriculture.

numbers.title: No bare numbers
numbers.body: Every value shows its context, uncertainty, provenance and the influences behind it.

scenarios.title: Compare, don't judge
scenarios.body: Cropstar shows possibilities and consequences. The decision remains yours.

why.title: Always an answer to “why”
why.body: Anything displayed also names the influences behind it. Otherwise, it is not shown.

warnings.title: Warnings describe, they never prescribe
warnings.body: Alerts describe what is happening. What you make of it remains your decision.

explore.title: Water and nitrogen in interaction
explore.lead: Two levers as they actually occur in the field: the rain you get, and the manure you spread. Every number carries its uncertainty and explains itself. Nothing here tells you what to do.

provenance.headline: Highly simplified — not a complete simulation
provenance.detail: This illustration focuses solely on how water and nitrogen availability might interact in winter wheat. A real ecosystem simulation would also need to account for temperature, radiation, soil structure, root dynamics, disease and management history, among other factors. The numbers come from a hard-coded response surface; no model runs in the background.

inputs.title: Inputs
inputs.rainfallHelp: Rain from sowing to harvest. How much of it becomes plant-available is decided by your soil — not by the amount alone.
inputs.waterStorageHelp: Higher storage buffers dry periods. Here it is a simplified stand-in for available water capacity and rooting.
inputs.soilNitrogenHelp: Plant-available stock at the start of the season. A soil analysis would be a better source than an estimate.
inputs.manureHelp: Fresh matter applied. Around 5 kg of total nitrogen per tonne, of which roughly a third becomes plant-available this season. The rest builds humus and works in later years.
inputs.ceiling: Above 34 t/ha the supply exceeds the 170 kg N/ha from livestock manure that the nitrate action programme permits per hectare and year.

outputs.title: Results
outputs.coverNote: Fraction of soil shaded by the canopy at its peak (fCover).

diagnostics.waterStressNote: Days on which plant-available soil moisture sat below 40 % of the usable field capacity.
diagnostics.nDeficitNote: Days on which the crop would have needed more nitrogen than soil and manure could supply.
diagnostics.nExportNote: Derived from yield and crude protein, using a factor of 5.7.

drivers.title: Why do these results change?
drivers.sharedIntro: The four results respond differently to water and nitrogen. Each bar shows which influence explains more of the difference from its lower reference – not which one is more important or better.

explanations.yield: Yield needs both: water sustains growth and grain filling, while nitrogen enables the crop to build leaves and grain.
explanations.protein: Protein responds especially strongly to available nitrogen. More water may increase yield faster than nitrogen uptake, diluting the protein share.
explanations.cover: Water and nitrogen promote leaf area and stand density. When either is scarce, the canopy closes later or remains patchy.
explanations.height: Adequate water maintains the pressure needed for cell expansion; nitrogen supports new tissue. Limits to either supply slow height growth.

drivers.footnote: The shares combine rain and soil storage as water supply, and soil and manure as nitrogen supply. One supply is set to its lower reference while the other stays constant.
drivers.water: Water supply from rain and soil
drivers.nitrogenReference: a field without available soil nitrogen or manure

explore.drawingAria: Stylised winter wheat responding to water and nitrogen availability
explore.caption: Drawn at BBCH 75 — medium milk. The drawing follows the figures beside it: tiller number from ground cover, colour from nitrogen supply, droop from water supply, rooting depth from the days spent short of water. The pale dots in the soil are plant-available nitrogen.
explore.closing: Note what the toy deliberately refuses to do: mark one setting as the right one. Two farms can read the same bands and decide differently — because soil, rotation, livestock and marketing differ.

contact.lead: We connect observations from practice with soil, weather, crop development, satellite data and models. The result is a tool that helps farmers understand their ecosystem more deeply over time.
contact.body: It is developed together with farms — and open to further perspectives from farming, advisory services and research.
contact.subject: Build together
contact.privacy: No form, no tracking, no mailing list. Plain email — and your address stays in our inbox.

status.nowBody: Together with farms, we capture workflows, decisions and sources of information.
status.nextTitle: Capture the field as a story
status.nextBody: Observations and field records become a traceable history of each field.
status.thenBody: Weather, soil and satellite data reveal developments and their causes.
status.laterBody: A crop model helps explore how water, nutrients, weather, rotations and mixed cropping interact.
